correctness.rationale: Using the nondegenerate invariant trace form, every nonzero rank-one operator has form R(x)=B(b,x)a; direct expansion is exactly [a,b] in kb. The centralizer of a nonzero traceless 2x2 matrix has dimension one in odd characteristic; noncentral eigenvectors b are nilpotent and have a 2-dimensional line normalizer. Thus the solutions are exactly the central and nilpotent-normalizer families; R^2=B(a,b)R identifies the square-zero component and the unique idempotent scalings. Rational nilpotent lines form a conic with q+1 points; counting normalizer vectors and self-adjoint tensors proves 2q^3-q-1 and all refined counts. Projective Veronese and normalizer-bundle parameter spaces prove the reduced irreducible components. Exhaustive direct identity evaluation for all a,b nonzero over F3,F5,F7,F9 reproduces every count; finite checks support but do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The 2013 Pei–Bai–Guo classification already solves all weight-zero operators over complex sl2; the associated complex rank-one cases are credited. The assessed original contribution is the characteristic-not-two rational two-family description, the exact finite-field rank-one, square-zero, projection and component-intersection counts for every odd prime power, and the reduced two-component geometry. The complex matrix families up to scalar do not state these rational point counts or justify characteristic-three specialization. The finite-field, tensor and eigenfunctional searches yielded no exact dominating result. The assessment remains provisional because an unlocated general rank-one Lie Rota–Baxter theorem could subsume it.

value.rationale: Rank one is a canonical determinantal stratum of the Lie Rota–Baxter equations, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The two-component reduced geometric classification and exact odd-prime-power count provide a rational arithmetic refinement that differs from the earlier complex full classification. The equality between the square-zero component and the nilpotent normalizer family, and the exact q^2 projection count, reveal intrinsic operator-type information needed to understand finite-field solutions.
